- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast peak by 1–2% and add a slight downward slope to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0–0.3), model tends to underestimate upward momentum; increase forecast mean by 0.5–1.0% to capture mean reversion bias.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is volatile; add 0.3–0.8% to early forecast to account for sentiment-driven volatility.  
- When sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often fails to recognize momentum; increase forecast slope by 0.2–0.5% to reflect sentiment shift.  
- Avoid overfitting to recent history; if last 3–5 days show strong downward trend, don’t assume continuation; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to counteract mean reversion.
